Every hook below has three parts:

- **Spoken:** what you say in the first three seconds, about 12 words or fewer.
- **On-screen:** the overlay viewers read with the sound off.
- **Type:** one of five hook types, so you can test which works for your audience.

Where a hook needs a real figure, it shows `[ADD: your number]`. Use your own verified number. Never invent one.

## How to Write Hooks for Free (By Hand)

You don't need a tool to write good hooks. You need a structure. This is the same five-type method used for every hook on this page.

**Step 1: Write the positioning in one sentence.** Who is this video for, and what do they want or fear? Example: "New freelancers who are scared to raise their rates."

**Step 2: Write one hook of each type.**
- **Curiosity:** open a question the video answers. *"The one line I add to every invoice."*
- **Contrarian:** push against a common belief. *"Cheap rates aren't winning you clients."*
- **Stakes:** name what it costs to ignore this. *"Underpricing now makes every future raise harder."*
- **Result:** lead with a real outcome. *"I raised my rate `[ADD: your number]` and kept every client."*
- **Callout:** name exactly who it's for. *"New freelancers, send this before your next quote."*

**Step 3: Make it filmable.** Swap abstract words for an object or action you can show: an invoice on screen, a hand pointing at a number, a door opening. If you can't picture the first frame, rewrite the line.

**Step 4: Cut it to three seconds.** Say it out loud with a timer. Delete "so," "hey guys," and "today I want to."

**Step 5: Write the overlay separately.** Shorter than the spoken line, and able to stand alone on mute.

**A free prompt for any AI chat tool**

If you already use a free AI chatbot, paste this and fill the brackets:

> Write 5 hooks for a short vertical video about [topic] for [audience]. Use one of each type: curiosity, contrarian, stakes, result, callout. For each, give a spoken line under 12 words and a shorter on-screen text. Make every hook name a specific object, action, or situation. Do not invent statistics; write [ADD: your number] where a figure is needed.

Then edit the output with Steps 3 to 5. Free tools rarely get the specificity right on the first try, so expect to rewrite.

## How to Choose and Test Your Hooks

- **Match the hook to the payoff.** If the hook promises a trick, show it. Broken promises teach viewers to scroll past you.
- **Use only real numbers.** No verified figure yet? Use a curiosity or contrarian hook instead of a result hook.
- **Test one variable.** Write three hooks of different types for one video, film the body once, re-record only the first three seconds, and post on separate days at a similar time.
- **Read your native analytics.** Compare early retention and average watch time in each platform's dashboard. Note the winning type: `[ADD: your result]`. Lean into what wins, and keep testing one new type now and then.
